title: Shalom
summary: In this New Year's message, William Branham addresses the Church as the elect Bride of Christ, contrasting the gross darkness covering the world with the Light of God's revelation. He emphasizes that God reveals His events in heaven before they occur on earth, citing recent signs such as the moon's blackout and the pope's visit to Jerusalem as fulfillments of prophecy. Branham calls the Church to peace (Shalom) and to arise and shine in the midst of darkness.

title: His Unfailing Words of Promise
summary: William Branham preaches on the unfailing nature of God's promises, using Matthew 24:32-35 as his text. He discusses the signs of the times, including the fig tree representing Israel becoming a nation, and shares a personal testimony of his wife's miraculous healing from a tumor.

title: God's Word Calls For A Total Separation From Unbelief
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of total separation from unbelief, using biblical examples from Genesis, the Nazarite vow, and the life of Jesus to illustrate how God's Word separates light from darkness, faith from doubt, and believers from the world. He emphasizes that true believers must separate themselves from anything contrary to God's Word, including church traditions and worldly cares, to become a Bride prepared for Christ.

title: Looking Unto Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of looking unto Jesus as the Word of God for this hour, emphasizing that each generation must see Christ revealed in the promised Word. He contrasts those who see only tradition or criticism with those who, like the prophets and disciples, recognize the vindicated Word and find salvation, healing, and life.
themes: Word of God for the hour

title: Turn On The Light
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of accepting the present light of God's Word rather than living in the glare of past ages. He uses the analogy of the sun to illustrate how each age has its own revelation, and warns against rejecting the current light as the Pharisees did. He calls the church to mature with the light and prepare for the coming of Christ.

title: What Shall We Do With This Jesus Called Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between the trial of Jesus before Pilate and the spiritual condition of the modern church. He warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit's work and the vindicated Word of God, urging listeners to accept Jesus Christ before it is too late.

title: God Is His Own Interpreter
summary: William Branham preaches that God interprets His own Word through manifestation, using examples from Scripture such as Abraham, the virgin birth, and the ministry of Jesus. He emphasizes that in the last days, the same signs seen in the days of Sodom will be repeated among the spiritual seed of Abraham.

title: God's Provided Way for This Day
summary: William Branham preaches on God's unchanging way of providing for His people in every age, emphasizing that God always works through His Word and His chosen prophets. He calls believers to come God's way—through the new birth and the baptism of the Holy Ghost—rather than relying on human traditions or denominational systems. The sermon encourages persistent faith and crying out to God until His promises are vindicated.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Ghost
God's provided way for each age

title: The Patriarch Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, the father of faith, emphasizing that true Seed of Abraham believe God's Word regardless of circumstances. He uses examples from the Bible to show how Abraham's Seed possess the gates of their enemies through faith, and concludes with a prayer for the sick.
themes: Possessing the gates of the enemy

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical token of the blood of the lamb in Exodus 12, which prefigures the Holy Spirit as the required token for believers today. He emphasizes that without the baptism of the Holy Ghost, one cannot be identified with Christ and will face judgment.

title: Countdown
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of scientific progress from horse and buggy to astronaut to illustrate the spiritual progression of the church through justification, sanctification, and the baptism of the Holy Ghost. He declares that the church is now in the 'astronaut age,' where believers are empowered by the Holy Spirit to rise above creeds and denominations, awaiting the rapture. The sermon emphasizes that natural achievements are types of spiritual realities, and the countdown of church ages is complete, with the next event being the catching away of the Bride.
themes: the astronaut age of the church

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, using the account of the disciples on the road to Emmaus to illustrate how Christ reveals Himself through the Word and through the same works He did before His crucifixion. He emphasizes that God always fulfills His promises, and that believers must invite Him in to have their eyes opened to His presence and power today.

title: Then Jesus Came And Called
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing that Jesus comes in the darkest hour when all hope is gone. He contrasts the evidence of true faith—vindication of the Word in the hour—with outward signs like speaking in tongues or shouting. Branham encourages believers to recognize Jesus as the manifested Word and to believe for the impossible.
themes: Jesus comes in the darkest hour

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham teaches on the relationship between signs and the voice of God, using Moses and the burning bush as a primary example. He explains that God gives signs to attract attention, and then the voice of the sign speaks through His Word, often through a prophet. Branham applies this pattern to the present day, urging believers to recognize the signs of the times and heed the voice of God's vindicated Word.

title: Influences
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influences, using the biblical account of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how pride and irreverence lead to downfall. He warns against compromising with the world and emphasizes the need for holiness and reverence in the presence of God.
themes: Influence of godly vs. ungodly examples
Holiness and separation from the world

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples, such as the Greeks seeking Jesus and the encounter with the Samaritan woman, to illustrate that God manifests His Word through prophets and signs. Branham calls the church to recognize the present hour and the promised signs of the end times.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the virtue of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as the Syrophenician woman, Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and John the Baptist. He emphasizes that true faith is persistent, based on the Word of God, and overcomes all hindrances.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here Now
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 12:38-42, comparing the generation that rejected Jesus to the queen of Sheba who traveled far to hear Solomon's wisdom. He emphasizes that Jesus is greater than Solomon and that the Holy Spirit's work today is the sign of the resurrection for this adulterous generation.
themes: God's gift of the Holy Spirit

title: A Testimony On The Sea
summary: William Branham uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate the need for a genuine revival and warns against the dangers of denominationalism and the Ecumenical Council. He calls the church to return to the power of the Holy Ghost and a humble, separated life.

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical token of the blood in Exodus as a type of the Holy Spirit today. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the token of identification with Christ, the paid price for redemption, and that only those displaying this token will be saved in the coming exodus of the Bride from the church.

title: God Is Identified By His Characteristics
summary: William Branham preaches that God is identified by His characteristics, which are supernatural and vindicate His Word. He uses biblical examples like Moses, Balaam, and Jesus to show that true identification comes through God's supernatural signs, not just fundamental teaching. He emphasizes that in the last days, the Son of man will be revealed to the elect as in the days of Sodom.

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the relationship between God's signs and the voice that accompanies them, using the example of Moses and the burning bush. He emphasizes that God always sends a prophet with a sign to attract attention, and the voice behind the sign must be scriptural. Branham applies this to the present day, warning of judgment and calling for repentance.

title: The Investments
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of a businessman offering an 'Eternal Life Assurance' policy to discuss the rich young ruler's encounter with Jesus. He contrasts worldly investments with the eternal investment of faith, emphasizing that true life comes only through a personal relationship with Christ, not church membership or moral living.
themes: Rejection of Christ by the religious

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how a man's life can impact others for good or ill. He warns against pride and stepping outside one's God-given calling, and emphasizes the need for reverence, humility, and action in serving God.
themes: The Blood of Christ as our covering

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the biblical account of Greeks seeking Jesus and the encounters with Nathanael and the Samaritan woman to illustrate how Jesus identified Himself as the Word made flesh, discerning the thoughts of the heart. Branham urges believers to look forward to what God is doing now rather than clinging to past traditions.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
Looking forward to God's present work

title: Calling Jesus On The Scene
summary: William Branham preaches on the disciples' experience of calling Jesus during a storm, drawing parallels to the present-day revival and the need to call on Jesus in times of trouble. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must have faith in His Word and presence.
themes: The Word of God as interpreter

title: God Identifying Himself By His Characteristics
summary: William Branham preaches on how God identifies Himself through His characteristics, using examples from nature, the Old Testament, and the life of Jesus. He emphasizes that God's characteristics are supernatural and unchanging, and that believers today should be identified by the same characteristics as Christ.
themes: the Spirit of God vs. church spirit

title: He Was To Pass This Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Zacchaeus, emphasizing the importance of seeking Jesus despite obstacles and the transformative power of encountering the real Christ. He encourages believers to be persistent in their faith and to examine the Word for themselves.

title: The Voice Of The Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of God's signs and their accompanying voice, using the Exodus narrative as a type. He emphasizes that true signs from God are followed by a Scriptural voice, and that prophets are signs of impending judgment, calling the elect to readiness.

title: The Identified Christ of All Ages
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Louisville, Mississippi, emphasizing the need for unity and faith. He discusses the nature of God as the same yesterday, today, and forever, and how He identifies Himself through His Word in each age, often through a single anointed individual.

title: A Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom allegory where God's Word is on trial against the world, with Satan as prosecutor and the Holy Ghost as defense witness. He calls biblical witnesses like Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Joshua to testify that God keeps His promises, and offers his own testimony of God's faithfulness. The sermon challenges believers to trust God's Word despite delays or opposition.
themes: the Word of God as seed

title: The Identification of Christ in All Ages
summary: William Branham introduces his ministry in Birmingham, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that God identifies Himself through prophets in each age, and that true faith rests on God's unchanging Word.

title: Scriptural Signs Of The Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of recognizing Scriptural signs and voices in the last days, warning against living in the glare of past revivals and urging believers to heed the present-day message of God. He emphasizes that God sends signs to attract attention, followed by a Scriptural voice, and that the generation that rejects the sign goes into chaos.

title: Spiritual Amnesia
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual condition of the church, drawing from Amos 3 to warn against forgetting God's Word and holiness. He identifies 'spiritual amnesia' as a disease causing believers to lose their identity in Christ and adopt worldly ways.

title: A Court Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom allegory where God is on trial for breach of promise regarding His Word. The prosecuting attorney Satan calls witnesses Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient to testify that God's promises of healing have failed. The defense witness, the Holy Spirit, argues that the promises are only for true believers and that the witnesses have misinterpreted the Word.

title: And When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, emphasizing that even though Jesus had promised His resurrection and explained the Scriptures, they did not recognize Him. He draws parallels to the present day, urging believers to recognize God's fulfillment of His Word and not be blinded by tradition or intellectualism.

title: Then Jesus Came And Called
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing that Jesus comes in the darkest hour to bring hope and resurrection. He contrasts human faith with God's power, urging believers to trust God's Word even when circumstances seem impossible.

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of a paradox—something incredible but true—using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, Moses parting the Red Sea, Noah's flood, and David defeating Goliath. He emphasizes that God works through ordinary men who are in the line of duty and have faith in His Word, and warns against relying on human intellect and organization rather than the power of God.

title: Jesus Keeps All His Appointments
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus keeping all His appointments, using the story of the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner but failed to honor Him. He draws parallels to modern church revivals where Christ is invited but not truly welcomed, and emphasizes the need for repentance and recognition of His presence.
themes: the pyramid as a type of the Church

title: The Trial
summary: In this sermon, William Branham presents a courtroom drama where the Word of God is put on trial for breach of promise. The prosecuting attorney, Satan, calls witnesses Unbelief, Skeptic, and Impatience to testify that God's promises fail. The defense witness, the Holy Spirit, calls biblical figures like Noah, Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and Isaiah to show that God's promises are fulfilled in His timing. Branham concludes by testifying to his own calling and the revelation of the Son of man in the last days.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit
the revelation of the Son of man

title: A Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom-style sermon where the Word of God is put on trial. The prosecuting attorney (Satan) calls witnesses Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient to testify that God's promises have failed. The defense Witness (Holy Spirit) calls Noah, Abraham, and Moses to show that God's Word is always fulfilled in His timing.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Oddball
location: Pine Lawn Trailer Park, Prescott, Arizona
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of a 'nut' (oddball) to describe those who are called out from the world to serve Christ. He traces biblical figures like Noah, Moses, Elijah, and Paul, as well as reformers like Luther and Wesley, who were considered fools by their contemporaries but were used by God to hold the Church together. Branham encourages believers to embrace being 'odd' for Christ, threaded to the Word, and to separate from worldly systems.

title: The Unveiling of God
summary: William Branham preaches on how God has always veiled Himself throughout history, changing His form (en morphe) from the Pillar of Fire to Jesus Christ to the Holy Spirit, and now reveals Himself to His elect in the last days. He emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must accept His Word by faith even when they cannot fully understand it.

title: The Oddball
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of being considered a 'nut' or 'oddball' for Christ, drawing from 1 Corinthians 1:18-25 and 2 Corinthians 12:11. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Elijah, John the Baptist, Jesus, and Paul, as well as historical figures like Martin Luther and John Wesley, to show that those who stand on God's Word are often ridiculed. Branham encourages believers to be threaded to the Word rather than the world, and shares testimonies of healings and miracles as evidence of God's power.

title: The Identified Christ of All Ages
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever, emphasizing that God reveals Himself through His Word and identifies Himself in each age. He uses biblical examples to show that Christ is the Word made flesh and that the same signs and wonders are available today.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and the Syrophenician woman to illustrate how those who have encountered God's presence and heard His voice become unstoppable. He encourages the congregation to be persistent in their faith despite obstacles, criticism, or lack of understanding from others.

title: Who Is Jesus?
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast, sharing personal anecdotes and a dramatic retelling of the story of Zacchaeus to illustrate the importance of seeking Jesus despite obstacles and societal opinions.

title: God Has A Provided Lamb
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus from Mark 10, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He illustrates how Bartimaeus's persistent faith stopped Jesus, and draws parallels to modern faith, including a personal testimony of a woman's prayer being answered. The sermon concludes with an altar call, urging listeners to cry out to Jesus, the provided Lamb of God.
themes: Jesus as the Lamb of God

title: The Trial
summary: William Branham presents a courtroom drama where God's Word is put on trial. The prosecutor (the devil) calls witnesses—Unbeliever, Skeptic, and Impatient—who claim God's promises have failed. The defense witness (the Holy Spirit) counters by calling biblical witnesses like Noah, Abraham, and Moses, showing that God's Word is always fulfilled in His timing.

title: The Mighty God Unveiled Before Us
summary: William Branham explains why believers appear odd to the world, using biblical examples like Noah and Moses. He discusses how God veils Himself from unbelievers but reveals Himself to believers, and how the Holy Spirit continues to work in the present age.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit
the continuity of God's work through history

title: The Masterpiece
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of Michelangelo's statue of Moses to illustrate God's work in creating humanity as His masterpiece. He traces the fall of man and God's redemptive plan through the patriarchs, prophets, and ultimately Jesus Christ, the perfect Masterpiece. Branham emphasizes that Christ is the fulfillment of all Old Testament promises and the only means of redemption.

title: Private Interview
subtitle: 64-0705X
summary: William Branham interviews Sister Georgia Bruce, reassuring her of her salvation and the sealing of the Holy Ghost. He prays for her healing, emphasizing that Christ's blood covers her sins and that her desire to serve God is evidence of her faith.

title: The Feast Of The Trumpets
summary: William Branham teaches on the Feast of Trumpets from Leviticus 23, explaining why the Holy Spirit prevented him from preaching on the Seven Trumpets at this time. He reviews the revelation of the Seven Church Ages and Seven Seals, emphasizing that the Trumpets pertain to Israel, not the Church, and that the Church is in the Laodicean age awaiting the return of Christ.

title: Going Beyond The Camp
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of leaving man-made religious camps and traditions to follow Christ outside the camp, bearing His reproach. He contrasts the camp of God's Word with denominational camps, emphasizing that true sanctification comes through Christ's sacrifice and that believers must go beyond human reason and tradition to experience God's presence and power.
themes: Rejection of tradition for the Word

title: Broken Cisterns
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 2:12-13, comparing man-made denominational systems to broken cisterns that hold stagnant, polluted water, while God is the Fountain of Living Water. He warns against apostasy and the mark of the beast, urging believers to come out of denominationalism and drink freely from Christ, the smitten Rock.

title: The Future Home of the Heavenly Bridegroom and the Earthly Bride
summary: William Branham preaches on the future home of the Bride of Christ, explaining that the earth will be cleansed by fire and restored as the eternal dwelling place of God and His people. He draws parallels between the three stages of redemption for individuals (repentance, sanctification, Holy Ghost baptism) and the three stages of the earth's redemption (water baptism of Noah's flood, Christ's blood, and final fire).

title: Proving His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of proving God's Word, using the examples of the woman with the issue of blood and the Queen of Sheba. He emphasizes that God always keeps His promises and that faith must rest on the proven Word of God, not on human reasoning or scientific proof.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham opens a question-and-answer session at the Branham Tabernacle, addressing topics such as the interpretation of Matthew 24, the nature of false prophets, the gathering of the Bride at the Rapture, and the relationship between water baptism, the Holy Spirit, and salvation. He emphasizes the primacy of the Word as the test of truth and clarifies that water baptism is an outward symbol of regeneration, not the means of remission of sins.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including Christian living, marriage, the Holy Spirit, and the end times. He warns against deception by signs and wonders, emphasizing the importance of staying true to the Word of God.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including the Bride of Christ, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, speaking in tongues, marriage and divorce, and the resurrection. He emphasizes that the Bride comes from all over the world, that the Holy Spirit's evidence is a life in harmony with God's Word, and that believers should not force spiritual gifts but let the Spirit work as He wills.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers a series of written questions from the congregation on topics including the Bride, the Holy Spirit, miracles, the resurrection, angels, and the end times. He also shares personal anecdotes and teachings on spiritual warfare and obedience to the Holy Spirit.

title: The Identified Masterpiece of God
summary: William Branham speaks on God's masterpiece of creation, from Adam to Christ, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the perfect reflection of God's Word. He calls believers to be beaten and purified by the Holy Spirit to reflect Christ, warning against worldly social gospel and denominational divisions.

title: The Harvest Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of living by every Word of God, using the metaphor of bread and harvest to illustrate how spiritual life is sustained by God's Word alone. He contrasts natural bread with Jesus as the Bread of Life, and warns against adding or subtracting from Scripture.
themes: Living by every Word of God
Jesus as the Bread of Life
The danger of adding to or subtracting from Scripture
The unity of believers in Christ

title: Why It Had To Be Shepherd
summary: William Branham explores why the birth of Jesus was first revealed to humble shepherds rather than to the religious leaders and theologians of the day. He argues that God bypassed the proud and learned because their theological training blinded them to the simple, humble arrival of the Messiah. Branham draws parallels to the present day, warning that modern religious institutions may similarly reject God's Word when it does not fit their denominational expectations.

title: Who Do You Say This Is?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question asked when Jesus entered Jerusalem: 'Who is this?' He contrasts the world's confusion and tension with the need to recognize the Messiah as the anointed Word for the hour, warning that many reject God's answer to their prayers because it doesn't fit their expectations.
